---
title: "Heat map"
page-layout: full
params:
  data_path: ""
---

```{r}
#| output: false
library(leaflet)
library(leaflet.extras)

# One row per grid cell, with n as the number of stream points that fell in it.
d <- readRDS(params$data_path)

# See detail.qmd for why this is not a single option: leaflet takes digits
# through htmlwidgets' serializer, and at 7 significant digits a coordinate is
# written with five decimals, which is the grid this data is already on.
widget_digits <- function(w, digits = 7) {
  if (is.null(attr(w$x, "TOJSON_FUNC", exact = TRUE))) {
    attr(w$x, "TOJSON_ARGS") <- list(digits = digits)
  } else {
    attr(w$x, "TOJSON_FUNC") <- function(x, ...) {
      jsonlite::toJSON(
        x,
        digits = digits, auto_unbox = TRUE, force = TRUE,
        null = "null", na = "null",
        time_format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS6", ...
      )
    }
  }
  w
}
```

```{=html}
<style>
/* The widget is emitted with a fixed pixel height. Overriding it here rather
   than at creation keeps the map filling whatever the frame gives it, which
   is what the iframe in index.html hands over. */
.html-widget.leaflet, .leaflet-container {
  height: calc(100vh - 7rem) !important;
  width: 100% !important;
}
</style>
```

```{r}
leaflet(d) |>
  addTiles(group = "OSM") |>
  addProviderTiles("OpenTopoMap", group = "Topo") |>
  addLayersControl(
    baseGroups = c("OSM", "Topo"),
    options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)
  ) |>
  addHeatmap(
    lng = ~lng, lat = ~lat, intensity = ~n,
    radius = 2, blur = 5, max = 0.05
  ) |>
  widget_digits()
```
